1#main: The place of its affixing, how it is affixed, and its blessing. In it are 6 seifim. When he comes to affix it, he places it in a tube of reed or of any matter and affixes it in its place; and he recites the blessing "...who commanded us to affix a mezuzah." And he does not recite a blessing at the time of writing. (And one who affixes two or three mezuzot recites one blessing for all of them) (Beit Yosef in the name of a responsum of the Rashba).
2#main: What is the place of its affixing? Within the hollow of the doorway, on the tefach adjacent to the outside (and if he changed, it does not invalidate, provided he place it in the doorpost itself) (Tur), at the beginning of the upper third of the height of the doorway; and if he affixed higher than this, it is valid—provided he distance it from the lintel a tefach. And he must affix it on the right of one entering. (And there is no difference whether he is left-handed or not) (in Mordechai, beginning of Hilchos Ketanim). And if he affixed it on the left, it is invalid.
3#main: One who divides his house in two, and in each part is a doorway open to the public domain, and in the dividing partition is a doorway from one to the other—at the place where he makes the hole in the threshold where the hinge of the door turns and he sets the doors, that is the house; and on the right of the way one enters, he affixes it.
4#main: How does he affix it? He nails it with nails in the doorpost of the doorway, or digs a hole in it and affixes it therein; and he should not dig deeply a tefach in depth, for if he did so it is invalid.
5#main: If he affixed it in the doorposts of the doorway while it was still detached and afterward attached it to the doorway—it is invalid.
6#main: It must stand upright—its length along the length of the doorpost; and he should intend that Shema—that is, the end of the rolling—be toward the outside. {Rama: And so they practice (Beit Yosef). But some say it is invalid standing upright; rather it must lie with its length along the width of the doorpost (Tur and poskim in the name of Rabbenu Tam). And the meticulous satisfy both views and place it on a slant diagonally (Tur, Hagahos Maimoniyos, Maharil, and Terumat HaDeshen siman 52); and so it is proper to practice, and so they practice in these lands—and one should intend that the head of the mezuzah, namely Shema, be toward the inside and the last line toward the outside.}
